segments.he: וְהַשָּׁחוּל וְהַכָּסוּל וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵיזֶהוּ כָּסוּל וְאֵיזֶהוּ שָׁחוּל? שָׁחוּל — שֶׁנִּשְׁמְטָה יְרֵיכוֹ, כָּסוּל — שֶׁרַגְלוֹ אֶחָד בְּתוֹךְ הַכֶּסֶל, וְרַגְלוֹ אֶחָד עַל גַּבֵּי הַכֶּסֶל. תָּנָא: הַשָּׂרוּעַ וְהַקָּלוּט — שָׂרוּעַ שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּרְבֵּב לוֹ יְרֵיכוֹ, קָלוּט — שֶׁרַגְלָיו קְלוּטוֹת כְּשֶׁל חֲמוֹר וּכְשֶׁל סוּס.
segments.en: The mishna teaches: «Or the shaḥul, or the kasul» may be slaughtered. In this regard, «the Sages taught: What is» the «kasul and what is» the «shaḥul?» The «shaḥul» is an animal with «a thighbone that was dislocated.» The «kasul» is an animal that is irregular in «that one of its legs is inside the loin,» i.e., in its proper place, «and» in «one of its legs» the bone is dislocated and is «above the loin.» It is «taught» in a baraita: What are «the saru’a and kalut» mentioned in the Torah (see Leviticus 22:23) among the animals disqualified from being sacrificed? The «saru’a» is one «whose thigh is longer» than the other; the «kalut» is one «whose» hooves on «its legs are closed like» those «of a donkey and like» those «of a horse.»
